r1_risk_change: Each outcome's 2024 rate as a ratio to its 2019 rate, under every denominator it can be paired with, Spain, all roads, with 95% intervals that allow for ordinary year-to-year variation; road fuel sold stands in for distance driven. Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; INE, Estadística Continua de Población; DGT, Censo de conductores 2014–2025; DGT registered vehicle fleet; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos.
l2_observed_over_trend: Observed deaths within 30 days as a ratio to the pre-pandemic trend of each measure (fitted to 2019, projected from 2020), with the trend's 95% prediction range shaded from 2020, Spain, 2010–2024; a year outside the shading is outside the trend's range. Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; DGT registered vehicle fleet; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos.
l1_trend_projection: Deaths within 30 days, Spain, 1993–2024 (road fuel from 1996), against segmented trends fitted up to 2019 and projected from 2020 with 95% prediction intervals; the middle panel counts the occupant deaths of motorcycles, cars, vans, trucks and buses, and the trends of the two rates are converted back into deaths. Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; DGT registered vehicle fleet; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos.
l4_km_against_fuel: Interurban deaths within 30 days as a ratio to a trend fitted to 2008–2019 and projected from 2020, per measured vehicle-kilometre and, as a check, over national road fuel sold, with the trend's 95% prediction range shaded, Spain, 2010–2023; the kilometres leave out roads run by municipalities and other bodies, which account for 8.7% to 11.2% of interurban deaths (2016–2024). Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos; Ministerio de Transportes y Movilidad Sostenible, Anuario Estadístico 2023.
l3_frequency_severity: Deaths within 30 days per tonne of road fuel sold (petrol plus diesel), split into injury crashes per tonne and deaths per injury crash (top) and into people admitted to hospital per tonne and deaths per admission (bottom), indexed to 1996 = 100, Spain, all roads, 1996–2024; each pair multiplies to deaths per tonne, and the two pairs divide its fall differently. Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos.
m1_season_profile: Deaths within 30 days, road fuel sold (petrol plus diesel), petrol sold and toll-motorway traffic per kilometre by month, each divided by its year's mean month and averaged over 2014–2024 (2020, 2021 left out), Spain; petrol and toll motorways cover only part of all traffic, and toll traffic is a daily average where the other series are monthly totals. Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos; Ministerio de Transportes y Movilidad Sostenible, tráfico en autopistas estatales de peaje.
m2_month_effects: Deaths within 30 days in each month against the average month of the same year, raw and per tonne of road fuel sold, Spain, 2014–2024 (2020, 2021 left out), with 95% intervals; the raw panel compares monthly totals, not adjusted for the number of days in a month. Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos.
m3_lockdown: Change in deaths within 30 days and in three measures of road use (road fuel sold, petrol sold, toll-motorway traffic per kilometre) in each month of 2020 against the mean of the same month in 2017–2019, Spain; the state of alarm began on 14 March 2020. Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos; Ministerio de Transportes y Movilidad Sostenible, tráfico en autopistas estatales de peaje.
a3_sex_ratios: Men's rates divided by women's among private-car drivers (taxis and ride-hailing cars excluded), by age: involvement in injury crashes and death within 30 days per licence holder, and death per driver involved, Spain, 2022–2024 pooled, with 95% intervals. The estimates per kilometre are given in the text. Source: DGT, Accidentes con víctimas, tablas estadísticas 2014–2024; DGT, Censo de conductores 2014–2025. n = 285,327 drivers involved.
f1_speed_severity: Deaths within 30 days per 100 injury crashes in which the police recorded inappropriate speed, as a ratio to the same rate in the other injury crashes on the same type of road, Spain outside Catalonia and the Basque Country, 2016–2023 pooled, with 95% intervals that allow for year-to-year variation (for the adjusted ratio, also for the differences between road types). Source: DGT, Informe temático Factor Velocidad 2014–2023; DGT, Ficheros de microdatos de accidentes con víctimas 2016–2024. n = 45,192 crashes with inappropriate speed recorded.
f2_factor_shares: Injury crashes in which the police recorded each factor, as a share of all injury crashes on interurban roads and on urban streets, Spain outside Catalonia and the Basque Country, 2014–2023; a line breaks where the share rises by more than 25% or falls by more than 20% in a year, or a year has fewer than 200 crashes. Source: DGT, Informe temático Factor Velocidad 2014–2023.
c3_speed_status: Drivers involved in injury crashes by the police record of a speed infraction, Spain, all roads, 2014–2024; the share with no speed status recorded changes in 2016, which shifts every share below it. Source: DGT, Accidentes con víctimas, tablas estadísticas 2014–2024. n = 1,794,406 drivers.
s1_forest_fatal: Odds ratios for at least one death in an injury crash, by crash circumstance, from a logistic regression that also includes the year, against reference levels (hollow markers), with 95% intervals, Spain, 2016–2024; zone and road type describe one location between them and are read together; levels that record a missing value are in the model but not drawn. Source: DGT, Ficheros de microdatos de accidentes con víctimas 2016–2024. n = 875,013 crashes.
s2_adverse_conditions: Odds ratios for at least one death in an injury crash under each adverse condition shown, against its reference level, in the full model and 7 variants that drop a correlated variable or fit one kind of road alone, Spain, 2016–2024, with 95% intervals; a missing row is a level the variant does not contain. Source: DGT, Ficheros de microdatos de accidentes con víctimas 2016–2024. n = 875,013 crashes.
dr1_involved_per_km: Car drivers involved in injury crashes in Spain in 2024 per kilometre driven by drivers of the same age, as ratios to drivers aged 45–64; kilometres by age from the EMEF's working-day profile applied to Spain's population and scaled to DGT's car kilometres. The grey bands are sensitivity ranges, not intervals: other regional profiles, the licence-calibrated transfer, other treatments of trip distances, other survey years, professionals' work driving, the older sample's employment and the age mix of non-working days. The rows for 65–74 and 75 and over rest on assumptions splitting the 65+ kilometres (Madrid survey ratios or licence holding) and carry no point estimate. Source: DGT, Accidentes con víctimas, tablas estadísticas 2014–2024; ATM, Idescat and Institut Metròpoli, Enquesta de mobilitat en dia feiner 2022–2024; CRTM, Encuesta Domiciliaria de Movilidad 2018 (Powered by CRTM); DGT, Kilómetros anualizados recorridos por el parque móvil 2024; INE, Estadística Continua de Población. n = 96,526 drivers involved.
dr2_killed_per_involved: Private-car drivers who died within 30 days per 1,000 involved in an injury crash, by age, Spain, 2024, with 95% intervals; no measure of driving enters the rate. Source: DGT, Accidentes con víctimas, tablas estadísticas 2014–2024. n = 96,526 drivers involved.
v1_per_vehicle_vs_per_km: Vehicles of each type involved in fatal crashes (deaths within 30 days) per 100,000 circulating vehicles (left) and per billion vehicle-kilometres (right), Spain, 2022; per kilometre only the lead of motorcycles is clear of the 95% intervals of the types below, some of which overlap (intervals in the rates table). Source: DGT, Accidentes con víctimas, tablas estadísticas 2014–2024; DGT, Kilómetros recorridos estimados a partir de la ITV 2022.
p1_points_series: Monthly road deaths within 30 days, Spain, January 2000 to November 2007, with a fitted segmented regression and two counterfactuals without the points-based licence of 1 July 2006: the fitted model with its change set to zero, and the same with one straight pre-trend, which gives the larger drop. Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024. n = 38,852 deaths.
p2_july_placebos: Estimated change in the level of monthly deaths at 1 July 2006 and at every other July of 1998–2018 whose window avoids July 2006 and the pandemic, each from the same segmented regression on 60 months before and 17 after, Spain, with model-based 95% intervals, which these placebos show to be too narrow; the filled marker is July 2006. Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024. n = 15 fits.
d1_missingness: Share of crashes with a value recorded in each field of the DGT crash records, by year, Spain, 2016–2024; a value counts as missing when it is empty, 999 (not specified), 998 (not applicable), an explicit unknown code or a placeholder (KM 9999, and 1000 in 2019; CARRETERA 'No inventariada'; COD_MUNICIPIO 00000). CONDICION_VIENTO is a presence flag: DGT's dictionary codes its absence as an empty cell, so its low share recorded means no strong wind, not missing data. Source: DGT, Ficheros de microdatos de accidentes con víctimas 2016–2024. n = 875,013 crashes.
cat1_fatal_by_road: Fatal crashes as a share of crashes with a death or serious injury, by road type, Catalonia, 2010–2023, with 95% intervals; groups of fewer than 30 crashes are left out. Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury. n = 24,478 crashes.
cat2_fatal_by_speed_limit: Fatal crashes as a share of crashes with a death or serious injury, by posted speed limit (the limit signposted on the road, not a measured speed), Catalonia, 2010–2023, with 95% intervals; groups of fewer than 30 crashes are left out. Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury. n = 24,478 crashes.
cat3_fatal_by_unit: Fatal crashes as a share of crashes with a death or serious injury, by type of road user or vehicle involved, Catalonia, 2010–2023, with 95% intervals; groups of fewer than 30 crashes are left out. Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury. n = 24,478 crashes.
cat4_fatal_by_crash_type: Fatal crashes as a share of crashes with a death or serious injury, by crash type, Catalonia, 2010–2023, with 95% intervals; groups of fewer than 30 crashes are left out. Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury. n = 24,478 crashes.
cat6_crashes_by_year: Recorded crashes with at least one death or serious injury, Catalonia, 2010–2023; counts of recorded crashes, not rates. Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury. n = 24,478 crashes.
bcn1_severity_by_road_user: People seriously or fatally injured as a share of the people in recorded crashes with a recorded injury outcome, by road-user role and vehicle type, Barcelona, 2025, with 95% intervals; groups of fewer than 30 people are left out. Source: Ajuntament de Barcelona, Guàrdia Urbana crash records. n = 15,848 people.
bcn2_severity_by_age: People seriously or fatally injured as a share of the people in recorded crashes with a recorded injury outcome, by age band, Barcelona, 2025, with 95% intervals; groups of fewer than 30 people are left out. Source: Ajuntament de Barcelona, Guàrdia Urbana crash records. n = 15,848 people.
bcn4_crash_severity_by_type: Crashes with at least one death or serious injury as a share of recorded crashes, by crash type, Barcelona, 2025, with 95% intervals; types of fewer than 30 crashes are left out. Source: Ajuntament de Barcelona, Guàrdia Urbana crash records. n = 7,741 crashes.
ml1_test_auc: ROC-AUC of each model, of the descriptive table it was compared with and of a baseline that gives every case the same probability, on test records not used to build them (Catalan crashes of 2023; Barcelona records of October–December 2025), with 95% intervals for the models. Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury; Ajuntament de Barcelona, Guàrdia Urbana crash records. n = 7,775 test records.
ml2_calibration: Observed share with the outcome against mean predicted probability in equal-size groups of test records (Catalonia crash-severity model: 10 groups, Catalan crashes of 2023; Barcelona person-severity model: 5 groups, Barcelona records of October–December 2025); on the diagonal, predicted probabilities match observed shares. Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury; Ajuntament de Barcelona, Guàrdia Urbana crash records. n = 5,781 test records.
ml3_importance_catalonia_crash_severity: The 10 variables the Catalonia crash-severity model relies on most: the mean fall in its ROC-AUC on the test records (Catalan crashes of 2023) when each variable is randomly shuffled, over 30 shuffles, with one standard deviation either side. Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury.
ml3_importance_barcelona_person_severity: The 10 variables the Barcelona person-severity model relies on most: the mean fall in its ROC-AUC on the test records (Barcelona records of October–December 2025) when each variable is randomly shuffled, over 30 shuffles, with one standard deviation either side. Source: Ajuntament de Barcelona, Guàrdia Urbana crash records.
tr0_calculator_transfer: ROC-AUC of the calculator's model on crashes held out of its fitting (each year from the years before it, the last year, each province of Catalonia in turn, Barcelona city from the rest of Catalonia), with 95% intervals, beside the same model fitted and cross-validated in the test population (hollow). Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury.
tr1_catalonia_transfer: ROC-AUC of the original Catalonia crash-severity model, retired because it relied on a recording artefact, on records held out of its training (a later year, each province of Catalonia in turn, Barcelona city from the rest of Catalonia), with 95% intervals where computed, beside a model of the same kind trained and cross-validated in the test population (hollow). Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury.
tr2_dgt_transfer: ROC-AUC of the harmonised Catalonia model (restricted to the variables DGT records in the same way) on records held out of its training: later years and each province in the Catalan file, the same crashes in DGT records, and DGT records from Spain outside Catalonia, with 95% intervals where computed, beside a model of the same kind trained and cross-validated in the test population (hollow). Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury; DGT, Ficheros de microdatos de accidentes con víctimas 2016–2024.
tr3_province_auc: ROC-AUC of the harmonised Catalonia model, trained on the Catalan file, on DGT records of crashes with a death or serious injury within 24 hours in each province outside Catalonia, 2016–2024; provinces with at least 30 fatal and 30 non-fatal crashes, fatal crashes in brackets. Source: DGT, Ficheros de microdatos de accidentes con víctimas 2016–2024. n = 67,704 crashes.
sev1_predicted_observed: Crashes in Catalonia in which someone was killed or seriously injured, 2016–2023, on the roads the calculator offers. Each year was predicted by a model fitted only on the years before it. The crashes are split into ten equal groups by the model's prediction (about 1,161 crashes each), and separately by the table's. Each dot is the share of a group's crashes that were fatal (someone died within 24 hours), with its 95% interval, against the group's average prediction. Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury. n = 11,611.
